memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'You must keep the Israelites separate from things that make them unclean, so they will not die in their uncleanness for defiling my dwelling place, which is among them.'" - Lev 15:31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
At last, the reason. And it is not what we might have guessed.

My dwelling place, which is among them. That is why all of this mattered. The holy God had come down to live in the middle of a camp of ordinary people — in their neighbourhood, among their tents, near their children. And that nearness was breathtaking and dangerous at the same time.

These laws were not God keeping His distance. They were God making it possible to stay close. He wanted to dwell among them, so He taught them how to live near Him without being consumed.

Now consider where this leads. In Christ, God did not merely camp among us — He became one of us and lived among us (John 1:14). And then, more astonishing still, His Spirit came to dwell not beside His people but within them. Do you not know that your bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit? (1 Cor 6:19).

The dwelling place has moved. It is no longer a tent in the middle of the camp. It is you.

That is why holiness still matters — not to earn God's presence, but because He has already made His home in you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does God's nearness feel wonderful to you, or uncomfortable?
2. What difference does it make that His Spirit dwells in you?
3. What in your life would you change if you truly took that seriously?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You did not stay distant but came to dwell among Your people, and now within them by Your Spirit. Make me a fitting home for Your presence. Amen.
